heading: The concept
text: NASHA is a planned Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas: five core dishes and five core beers designed together so that each plate has a drink chosen for it, with non-alcoholic pairings given equal standing. It is a concept and a development system today, not an operating business.

heading: The opportunity (a hypothesis)
text: Hypothesis, untested: guests who already enjoy Indian food, Mexican food and craft beer may value a place where those traditions meet in dishes that feel like one cuisine, with the pairing explained simply. No demand data exists; the cheapest tests are listed in the risk table.

heading: The solution
text: A compact core menu cooked on a small set of stations (fryer, comal, char), a beer list built to match it, and a hall where the brewing is visible. The brewery is the last capital gate: food and demand come first, and host-brewery or collaboration paths can test beer with far less capital.

heading: The product
text: Core 5 food: Chicken 65 Totopos, Paneer Tikka Taco, Goat Birria, Gobi Taco, Butter Chicken and Roasted Poblano Quesadilla. Core 5 beer: Hefeweizen, Mexican-Style Lager, Vienna Amber, Pilsner, Witbier. All are design briefs; none has been cooked or brewed.

heading: What may make it different
text: The combination and the execution, not any single ingredient: pairing designed in from the start, a no-beef and no-pork kitchen as a clear constraint, and a development process that publishes what failed. Indian, Mexican, fusion, brewery and destination-hospitality businesses all exist in Austin; the market lessons are in the market view.

heading: Current stage
text: Concept and design blueprint, before any physical test. Nothing has been cooked, brewed, tasted by anyone outside the project, priced from real receipts or reviewed by a professional.

heading: What has been done
text: Concept and product system documented; the first home-kitchen test (Chicken 65 Totopos) designed with fixed pass and fail rules and prepared for cooking; economic model structure with provenance rules; operating, kitchen, brewery, guest-journey and space requirements drafted; risk register with cheapest tests; this private site.

heading: What has not been done
text: Nothing has been cooked, brewed, tasted by anyone outside the project, photographed as a real prototype, priced from real receipts or quotes, reviewed by a lawyer, brewer, chef or advisor, or sold. There is no site, no entity, no permit, no customer and no investor conversation.

heading: Capital strategy
text: Staged: pre-capital founder build, low-cost validation, commercial validation, site and design, build, opening. No fundraising amount is set; amounts will follow real quotes. Each stage is tied to the risk it removes and to gates that stop spending when evidence does not support it.

heading: Next proof points
text: Cook and document the first dish with receipts, weights, photographs and tasters' scores; repeat for the other four; compute real food costs; then, once funds exist, take the name to an attorney, scope the legal path for beer with food, and run a first lawful commercial pilot.

heading: Major risks
text: The name is in question (a same-name Austin restaurant has been reported); no dish is proven; margin, labor and throughput are unknown; the brewery is capital-heavy; the founder is the only team member today. Each risk has a cheapest test in the risk table.

heading: The founder
text: Ritesh Mamidi is building NASHA as a one-person project, using the pre-capital period to develop as much of the company as can be done without money: product system, economic model, operating blueprint, a private website and a data room, and personal home-kitchen testing. No hospitality, culinary or brewing credentials are claimed; the capability gaps are listed openly in the future-team view.
